title: 8 stencil-op color-probe oracle
purpose: Render an 8-cell 4x2 grid where each cell exercises one of the 8 NV2A stencil ops (KEEP/ZERO/REPLACE/INCRSAT/DECRSAT/INVERT/INCR/DECR). Per cell: clear stencil to 0x80, render an op-pass quad (color=BLACK, stencil func=ALWAYS, op applied to FAIL/ZFAIL/ZPASS, ref=0x40), then a probe quad with stencil func=EQUAL+ref=<expected post-op value>. The probe paints the cell's expected color (one of the 7 saturated RGB cube corners avoiding BLACK) when the post-op stencil matches the spec; if the op was mis-implemented the cell stays BLACK. Pure 0/255 RGB so byte-exact across renderers regardless of display gamma. v1 plan's Tier-2 readback proposal was rejected (Codex finding #7) because Metal's surface-download path skips the stencil aspect; this color-probe redesign keeps the verdict inside the visible drawable. Per the §4.10 spec, the chosen initial stencil 0x80 is intentionally in the no-overflow region for INCRSAT/DECRSAT/INCR/DECR; a separate XBE will exercise the saturation boundary at 0xFF/0x00. **TASK #14 PARTIAL FIX 2026-05-20 late evening:** Metal's pgraph_mtl_surface_clear hardcoded `desc.stencilAttachment.clearStencil = 0` instead of honoring the decoded stencil clear value (now fixed) -- eliminated deterministic op-value-mismatch failures. **TASK #14 FULL FIX 2026-05-20:** added clear-draw cross-queue synchronization in pgraph_mtl_surface_clear via [cmd waitUntilCompleted]. Root cause was a cross-queue race between s_render_queue (clears) and s_draw_queue (per-cell op_pass + probe_pass draws) -- the encodeWaitForEvent fence pattern used elsewhere did not serialize the clear-before-draw ordering on Apple Silicon as expected. The waitUntilCompleted hammer ensures each clear's load_action_Clear completes before the next draw reads stencil. Counterpart cross-queue fences (signal s_clear_done_event in surface.mm + mtl_draw_wait_clear_fence in draw.mm open_pass_ensure) remain in place as a soft guarantee. Perf cost is bounded -- retail games issue ~2-4 clears per frame so the host-side CPU stall is sub-ms per frame. After the fix the harness consistently selects an 8/8 frame (composite signal x total selector) and the rotation passes deterministically. GL and real-Xbox cells PASS unchanged.
